messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected — elevated tail latency on text-generation-prod (p95 spike). Pager triggered to on-call. Incident ID: INC-2026-03015-TG. Auto-opened runbook: /incidents/INC-2026-03015-TG.

maya: Acknowledged. I'm oncall and looking. First step: is this global or region-specific?

ryan: Metric snapshot: p50 ~ stable, p95 jumped from ~180ms -> ~1.2s in last 6m, overall throughput down ~28%. Error rate for 503s is ~0.4% (up from 0.01%). Spike correlates with queue depth on the tokenizer workers.

ana: Recent deploys? Anything rolled in last hour?

deploy-bot: deploy completed by ana at 1778999400 (commit: a7f3bde) — rollout to text-generation-prod finished ~12 minutes before alert.

maya: thanks. tagging @ana for triage. I'm starting a telemetry snapshot (logs/traces) and will attach link in a sec.

ana: looking at the rollout diff — small scheduler tweak that touches batching behavior. Hypothesis: new batching threshold causing large variable-sized batches for long prompts -> kv cache pressure.

ryan: logs: a few upstream connections showing long GC pauses on tokenizer instances, then backlog. Also seeing an increase in queuing latency on the request router.

ana: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily rollback scheduler change OR 2) route low-priority routes (embeddings, background-rerank) to the fallback cluster and reduce batch cap. Prefer non-rollout first. Maya, can you set traffic weight for low-priority routes to 10%? Command:
```
rictl traffic-route set --service text-generation-prod --route embeddings,rerank --weight 0.1
```

maya: running the command now.

maya: command executed. Confirmed weights updated. Also lowering max-batch-size on prod router to 64 from 256 to force smaller batches:
```
rictl config set --service text-generation-prod --max-batch-size 64
```

ryan: seeing immediate drop in queue depth on tokenizer workers. p95 trending down to ~600ms after 90s. Throughput recovering.

ana: good. I'm preparing a rapid revert for the scheduler change if we don't stabilize in 10-15m.

jordan: drafting status page + customer notification. Proposed public message: "We are investigating elevated latency for the Text Generation API impacting some requests. We have applied mitigations and are monitoring. No data loss. We will update within 30 minutes." Want to confirm impact scope before publishing — are any customers fully rate-limited or receiving 503s?

maya: partial 503s observed but limited to <1% of requests and concentrated on long-context jobs. Most customers seeing degraded latency rather than outright failure.

jordan: ok draft for statuspage: 
- Impact: Increased latency for Text Generation API (some long-context requests may see errors)
- Scope: small subset of requests, not all customers
- Action: routing and batch size adjustments applied
- Next update: 30 minutes or on recovery

jordan: also prepping a customer support template: "We identified an issue causing increased response times for long-text generation; our engineers have applied mitigations (routing & batch caps) and expect restoration in ~20–40 minutes. If you continue to see errors, please share request IDs and we'll prioritize investigation."

matt: I'm coming on shift for handoff. Maya — handoff in 5. I'll take over if this persists past the next update.

sara: adding a quick internal exec blurb for ops-channel: "TL;DR: transient p95 spike due to batching change; mitigations in flight (route low-priority traffic off, cap batch size). Risk low for data loss. Estimated recovery 20–40m."

ryan: p95 now at ~320ms and trending toward baseline. Error rate down to 0.05%. Queue depth near normal.

ana: canceling revert for now, will hold change paused and run a safer threshold tweak tomorrow. Will open a follow-up PR with gradual rollout and more telemetry.

jordan: publishing status update to status.redwood.com now.

deploy-bot: status update posted: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2026-03015-TG-update1 (public).

maya: closing notes: mitigation worked; stabilization confirmed. Follow-ups: postmortem to include root cause (batching throttle interaction), rollout gating for scheduling changes, improved canary rules for batch-size-sensitive services, and a customer comms timeline. Assigning postmortem to ana + ryan.

ana: ack. I'll own the postmortem.

matt: took handoff. If anything regresses, I'll escalate. Great work team :thumbsup:

jordan: final customer-facing update queued: "Mitigation applied and performance returning to normal. We will follow up with a detailed postmortem and preventative actions. If you continue to be impacted, contact support with request IDs."

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-03015-TG marked as "investigated" (mitigated) at 1779000780. Postmortem required.
